items.reason: The way back out is now rehearsed by a machine instead of by a runbook nobody ran: `npm run revert:drill` proves the tree is green, seeds a real one-line fault on a seam with an ADR behind it, times which gate layer catches it, then removes it and asserts the file is byte-for-byte what it was; .github/workflows/revert-drill.yml fires it every Thursday and on demand, goes red when a seed survives every layer or when an anchor has drifted, and publishes the dated row into a trail issue plus a 90-day artifact — and the runbook now also states what a promote does NOT take back (uploaded conversions, sent mail, Firestore docs in a new shape, crons that fired), which is the question that decides promote versus fix-forward.

docs/agent-index.md states every spec in .claude/agents/ in the three facts a caller needs — what it is for, what it may assume about the tree and the handoff (including the two that are properties of the tree rather than the prompt: the finish reviewer has no browser, the applier must not touch git), and what it returns — routed from docs/task-index.md and AGENTS.md, and held true by test-unit/agent-index.test.mjs inside test:unit -> check:ci -> pre-push, so a spec that lands with no row, a row naming a spec that is gone, or a spec whose `name:` stops matching its filename is a red build.

The rule is complete and blocking on every path the repository controls (rubric A5 over origin/master..HEAD, in agent-review.yml and in check:ci/pre-push), and the narrating subjects still land because the Ascent lane commits in a linked worktree that has no `.husky/_` — husky's shim directory is untracked, so git runs NO hook here whatever core.hooksPath says, and a post-hoc gate cannot unwrite a subject; the two files scripts/commit-check.mjs documents as the fix (.husky/commit-msg, .husky/prepare-commit-msg) are refused to this session because .husky/ is a permission-gated path, and even committed they would not fire in a hookless worktree, so the decision left is the operator's: track husky's shims so lane commits run the hook at all.

Needs network: pinning means asking GitHub what each tag points at right now, and the repository already ships that exact path — `npm run actions:pin` resolves every tag to its digest, rewrites the workflows, and writes STRICT = true and RATCHET.pinned back into scripts/actions-pin.mjs in the same pass, so both halves land in one diff; there is nothing left to build offline and an invented SHA would break the workflows rather than pin them.

Needs a run to mint the baseline: a speed budget that fails on a regression has to record today's numbers first (a `next build` for route weight, a Playwright or Lighthouse pass for paint), and this session has no shell, no build and no test runner — a ceiling I invented would be decoration, and a gate wired into check:ci with no baseline would turn every build red.

Needs key provisioning: signing requires a key per lane and a git identity configured where the lane runs, both outside this repository and outside a session that cannot run git; a verifier committed now would report 0% coverage forever and would not make one commit verifiable, which is the gap the item names.

lessons: In this organization's Ascent lanes the worktree has no `.husky/_` (husky's shim directory is untracked), so git runs no hook there whatever the shared core.hooksPath says — that, and not a missing rule, is why commit-subject and attribution rules keep being bypassed by lane commits. Any fix that lives in a hook cannot be landed from a lane: `.husky/` and `.claude/` are permission-gated paths for these sessions.

When a session cannot execute anything, put new unattended checks in their own reporting-rung workflow rather than into the blocking chain: an untested script in `check:ci` risks a red build for everyone, while the same script on a weekly schedule can only fail its own job — which is also the rung ADR-0007 prescribes for a check that does not pass on the tree yet.

A drill that shells out to the project's own gates must set spawnSync `maxBuffer` explicitly: Node's 1 MB default truncates a large suite's output and exits the child non-zero, which a detection drill would faithfully report as the fault being caught. Prove the unseeded baseline is green first for the same reason.

This repository answers 'which document?' with docs/task-index.md and holds it true with a unit test; the same shape transfers cleanly to any other tacit choice a run makes at the start (here, which subagent) — an index plus a test that fails when an artefact lands without a row is cheaper and more durable than prose asking people to remember.
